_note: Words That Don't Exist in English be like. Native word = real recording (Lingua Libre / Wiktionary pronunciation files on Commons); the English translation is read by a Piper AI voice, labelled on screen. Ranked 10 -> 1 by the number of English words in the shortest honest translation (counted by fetch_untrans.py).
title: Words That Don't Exist in English be like

items.name: German
items.fact: English tried for centuries and gave up: since the 1890s it simply borrows the German word. The French have it too, but need a sentence.

items.name: Swedish
items.literal: according to the law (of the group)

credit.artist: uploader not named on the file page

items.fact: Swedes call it their national philosophy: the right amount of coffee, of work, of showing off. Legend says it comes from Vikings passing a horn of mead around the team: 'laget om', enough for everyone.

items.name: Japanese
items.fact: In Japan it is an everyday word: your ikigai can be your grandchildren, your garden or your job. The Venn diagram with four circles that went viral is a Western invention from 2014.

items.name: Russian

credit.artist: uploader not named on the file page

items.fact: Nabokov said no English word renders it: at its deepest it is a great spiritual anguish, at its lightest, boredom. Russian novels run on it.

items.name: Dutch
items.fact: A café can be gezellig, an evening, a person, even a chair. The Dutch rank it among the most important words in their language, and swear hygge is just the Danish copy.

items.name: Portuguese
items.fact: Portugal has a whole music genre built on it, fado, and Brazil celebrates a Day of Saudade on 30 January. You can feel saudade for a person, a city, or a time that never existed.

items.name: German
items.fact: German just glues two words together: Kummer, grief, plus Speck, bacon. The same trick gives Backpfeifengesicht, a face that is asking for a slap.

items.name: French
items.fact: It can be the thrill of a new city or the unease of a strange one. The French use it for both, which is why travel agencies sell it and homesick students complain about it.

items.name: Chinese
items.fact: In China you build guanxi for years, with dinners, gifts and favours, before you need it. Business schools in the West now teach it under its Chinese name.

items.name: Czech
items.translation: Torment at seeing your own misery.
items.fact: That definition is Milan Kundera's. He said he looked in vain for the word in other languages, and could not imagine understanding the human soul without it.
